final_candidates.decision_summary: Mutating the central hydrophobic core tryptophan to an aspartate introduces a buried negative charge that severely destabilizes native tertiary folding.
Substituting phenylalanine 40 with aspartate disrupts essential hydrophobic packing interactions, resulting in severe fold destabilization.
Introducing an aspartate at tyrosine 18 perturbs beta-hairpin core packing through desolvation and electrostatic penalties.

stop_reason.detail: High-confidence destabilizing mutations targeting the structural core have been identified, rendering additional iterative rounds unnecessary.

history.rationale: Trp17 is a critical hydrophobic core residue in the PsaE beta-barrel; introducing a charged aspartate severely destabilizes the hydrophobic packing and disrupts folding.
W17 is a central core aromatic residue crucial for fold stability; mutating to Asp introduces a buried negative charge that severely destabilizes folding.
Phe40 is deeply buried in the hydrophobic core of the beta-barrel; substitution with a charged aspartate causes severe steric and electrostatic clashes that disrupt folding.
F40 forms a key hydrophobic packing contact in PsaE; introducing an aspartate creates severe steric and electrostatic disruption.
Tyr18 forms conserved tertiary core contacts across the beta-sheets; mutating it to aspartate destabilizes the sheet interface and prevents stable tertiary structure formation.
Y18 pairs with W17 in the hydrophobic beta-hairpin core; Asp substitution disrupts core packing and beta-strand conformation.
Ile33 is a central core-facing hydrophobic residue on beta-strand 3; introducing a negatively charged carboxylate strongly destabilizes the fold.
I33 is buried within the interior beta-sheet structure, where Asp mutation strongly penalizes folding thermodynamics.
Phe48 contributes essential aromatic packing to the PsaE structural core; replacing it with aspartate disrupts the hydrophobic cluster and destabilizes folding.
F48 stabilizes the loop-to-sheet transition; inserting a charged Asp disrupts packing and fold stability.
Val38 is buried within the interior of the beta-sheet network; an aspartate mutation creates an uncompensated buried charge, destabilizing the protein.
V38 contributes to beta-strand hydrophobic interactions that are destabilized by charged carboxylate incorporation.
Leu55 is a hydrophobic residue stabilizing the C-terminal segment against the beta-sheet; Asp55 disrupts local hydrophobic interactions and fold stability.
L55 packs against the core; Asp substitution exerts significant desolvation and folding penalties.
Val24 resides on beta-strand 2 pointing into the hydrophobic interior; introduction of aspartate breaks strand packing and promotes unfolding.
V24 participates in strand packing; Asp introduces strong electrostatic destabilization.
Phe60 participates in anchoring the C-terminal region to the folded domain; substitution with aspartate eliminates hydrophobic packing and destabilizes the fold.
F60 provides C-terminal anchoring hydrophobic contacts disrupted by introducing an acidic residue.
Ile10 is located on beta-strand 1 participating in the core scaffold; mutation to aspartate introduces unfavorable electrostatic strain in the beta-sheet.
I10 stabilizes the N-terminal beta-strand; Asp substitution promotes local unfolding.
